newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds await Russia, more dollars next week.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds await Russia, more dollars next week.

text.p: Primary market activity slowed on Friday after a busy week.
The dollar sector has been particularly active, with retail-targeted deals dominating. Borrowers are taking advantage of a large number of dollar redemptions due on July 7, bankers said.
Institutional-targeted dollar issuance could resume next week, with a handful of bonds already in the pipeline.
Japan Finance Corp for Municipal Enterprises (JFM), guaranteed by Japan, plans a $400 million 10-year bond via Merrill Lynch and Tokyo-Mitsubishi International.
Bankers said spread talk was between 21 and 23 basis points over U.S. Treasuries notes.
Five-year dollars could also see supply.
"There is an opportunity for a five-year institutional deal but there is no specific transaction planned yet," a trader at a U.S. bank said.
On the emerging market side Russia is expected to launch its second dollar Eurobond next week. Roadshows end next Wednesday, and launch could come soon after.
Earlier, Russian deputy finance minister Mikhail Kasyanov said it would borrow at least $1.0 billion at a 10-year maturity. J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg are joint lead managers.
Bankers said spread talk was between 375 and 385 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes.
Also on the emerging market side, China will hold the London leg of its roadshow for a 500 million mark Eurobond on Monday.
